The symmetric pair attains the lower bound by minimizing the common max floor, including boundary a=0, d=2 and a≥1. The explicit real linear isometry preserves U. value.rationale: Johnson–Kania introduce the two-parameter Steinhaus visibility modulus as a natural geometric invariant but calculate it on nonatomic L1, where it never vanishes at positive radius. This full exact profile gives a motivated atomic benchmark, not merely a yes/no property-(S) counterexample: it computes the least radius hiding any prescribed distance, the sharp linear gain region, the saturation radius, and a canonical extremizer for every pair of parameters. The qualitative failure in the nonsmooth square was already known, and is not presented as new. These sharp thresholds may serve as test cases for atomic/nonatomic stability, local visibility and renorming comparisons.
